body:
## Goals

Build a trustworthy answer to **whether recent workflow history can predict the next software-development action usefully and cheaply—using a remote model or a local predictor**—before committing to a custom model or fine-tuning strategy.

- Predict the next **observed** action at the Oracle's actual end-of-turn boundary, using only information available then. This does not establish what the developer *should* do.
- Compare simple local baselines with **GPT-5.6 Luna as a remote replacement for the custom Oracle**, on identical independently held-out examples; preserve all 44 canonical label IDs. Custom training is conditional, not the default deliverable.
- Produce either a reproducible candidate ready for a separately scoped serving pilot, or a defensible stop decision. A negative result is a completed experiment.

“Clean room” means rebuilding the experimental assumptions, not discarding working code or claiming legal clean-room provenance. Reuse the existing taxonomy, serializer, and useful evaluation components after checking their contracts.

## Prerequisites — before evaluation or training

- Original transcript metadata must support reliable session identity, event order, and the chosen prediction boundary. The rendered training JSONL alone is insufficient: it drops session/step provenance.
- Inventory which sessions trained existing adapters and which evaluations have already influenced decisions. Existing #5/#12 holdouts are **development/diagnostic data**, not an untouched final test.
- Identify never-used complete sessions, or collect future sessions after freezing the protocol. Do not enable new recommendations during collection; record any existing recommendation exposure.
- Verify access to the exact remote API model `gpt-5.6-luna`, credentials, account rate limits, and current prices using a synthetic request at execution time. Documentation establishes model availability, not this account's entitlement. Do not silently substitute another model.
- Define the remote payload and approved data handling before sending private histories: only the current allowed request/history and canonical label descriptions, without credentials, raw transcripts, or unneeded code/path content. Apply the same redaction to all primary comparison arms. This plan update sends no private examples and makes no paid model calls.
- Freeze the taxonomy revision, target Mac, input budget, observation horizon, split policy, evaluation gates, and resource cap. Changes after results are inspected require a new protocol version.
- Keep private inputs and per-example evidence under ignored `data/`; public receipts contain aggregates and synthetic examples only.

## Assumptions to test first

| Assumption | Test / consequence if false |
|---|---|
| End-of-turn history contains enough signal before another request arrives. | Evaluate actual Stop-boundary examples. Never include the next user request. Weak results may justify a separately proposed prediction point after a request arrives; do not silently change the task. |
| We can reconstruct those boundaries reliably. | Replay a small set of original transcripts against observed Stop snapshots. Missing boundaries/provenance mean prospective collection, not invented timestamps or file-mtime splits. |
| Labels describe the intended target accurately. | Audit a stratified sample of mapped source events, especially rare/governance actions and known taxonomy failures (#2). Treat mappings as weak observed labels, not expert advice. |
| Repeated rows represent independent behavior. | Separate copied source events from legitimate repeated situations. Group copied/branched session families; report conflicting next labels for identical observable inputs rather than arbitrarily deleting them. |
| Luna can replace custom training at acceptable cost and latency. | Evaluate it early against the same local baselines; measure accuracy, p95 request-to-result time, failures, and billed tokens. A remote win can end the training effort; a remote loss does not prove the task impossible. |
| Outbound API use fits the product. | Confirm permitted payloads, provider retention, connectivity requirements, and spend limits. If remote use is unsuitable, retain the local route without changing the evaluation task. |
| Either predictor can preserve the product contract. | Score over the canonical label space without hidden candidate retrieval; verify unsupported classes are reported, not removed. Confidence abstention and the semantic `no_action` label remain distinct. |

**Status:** proposed, not started. **Created:** 2026-09-09 UTC. **Updated:** 2026-09-09 UTC — Luna replacement arm added at operator request. **Owner:** unassigned. **Triage:** effort 3/5, complexity 3/5, risk 2/5; provisional, five phases. **Reversibility:** Easy for isolated local work and synthetic API probes; transmitting private data cannot be undone. A live remote backend or retrain remains a later Costly decision with its own rollback. This issue authorizes no deployment or campaign execution by itself.

| What was just completed | What's next |
|---|---|
| Source-grounded recon and Luna API documentation check; no new model training or inference. | Verify prediction boundaries, provenance, and remote prerequisites; then freeze the comparison protocol. |

**Contents:** [Grounding](#grounding-and-scope) · [Remote replacement](#gpt-56-luna-replacement-arm) · [Execution](#execution--one-ordered-sequence) · [Decision gates](#decision-gates) · [Completion](#completion-and-boundaries)

## Grounding and scope

Recon at `710c32dcfcfff020d34427fdbc6ba4defdc4304e`, plus explicitly uncommitted #12 experiment files:

| Existing seam | Consequence for this plan |
|---|---|
| [Extractor](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/Needle-fork/blob/710c32dcfcfff020d34427fdbc6ba4defdc4304e/utils/corpus/extract_claude_transcripts.py#L110) produces every-tool examples and hashes transcript paths for session IDs. | A copied file can acquire a new split identity; every-tool examples are not end-of-turn examples. |
| [Serializer](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/Needle-fork/blob/710c32dcfcfff020d34427fdbc6ba4defdc4304e/utils/corpus/serialize.py#L74) is shared, but rendered rows omit provenance and target reasoning names the answer. | Reuse input rendering; preserve provenance separately and prohibit target reasoning/tool metadata as features. |
| [Stop hook](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/Needle-fork/blob/710c32dcfcfff020d34427fdbc6ba4defdc4304e/utils/hooks/oracle_stop_hook.py#L67) later scores the first action after its saved history. | Define the same decision point and observation horizon offline. No later action is a censored observation, not automatically `no_action`. |
| [Inference worker](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/Needle-fork/blob/710c32dcfcfff020d34427fdbc6ba4defdc4304e/utils/hooks/oracle_infer.py#L37) projects results into `{label, why}` recommendations. | Preserve that external shape; internal prediction need not generate tool-call JSON. |

[Latest #12 results](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/Needle-fork/issues/12#issuecomment-5597080101) are useful diagnostic evidence, not proof of a single numerical or retrieval cause. Current local scoring still accepts two separate tool-call blocks and invalid argument shapes in synthetic probes. Reuse requires verification; “a rebuilt harness” is not a blanket certificate. This issue does not replace #12's native-engine investigation or #9's governance-data work.

## GPT-5.6 Luna replacement arm

**Preferred first bet:** buy prediction from Luna if it clears the usefulness and operating gates, rather than building and maintaining a custom model. This preserves the Oracle's user-facing function while replacing its predictor. It is an input/output-compatible adapter, not a `.cact` file swap or a promise that network behavior matches local inference.

The [official model page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-luna) lists `gpt-5.6-luna`, Responses API access, structured outputs, and `reasoning.effort=none` support. Published token rates checked 2026-09-09 are $0.20/M input and $1.20/M output. Recheck before execution; pin a snapshot if available, otherwise record the alias, returned model identifier, date, prompt/schema hashes, and settings and acknowledge version drift.

Use one independent Responses request per example, with `store=false`, no conversation continuation, no tools, browsing, retrieval, or code execution. Supply the same prediction-time information as the local arms plus the canonical 44-label descriptions. Start zero-shot with reasoning effort `none`; permit at most one development-selected alternative prompt using training-only examples. No test examples enter prompts and no retries hunt for a correct answer. Keep prompt text fixed across rows except for the permitted input.

Request an ordered list of three distinct canonical label IDs (or an explicit empty abstention), validate it locally, and map it to the existing `{label, why}` recommendations using canonical templated descriptions. Score first label as top-1 and the list as top-3. Treat refusals, incomplete output, duplicates, and invalid labels separately; [structured outputs do not eliminate refusal handling](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs). Do not ask for chain-of-thought or treat self-reported confidence as a calibrated probability. Untrusted request text is data, not permission to change the schema or call tools.

“Drop-in” applies at `oracle_infer.py`'s prediction boundary: a future pilot adds an explicit backend/model setting in the existing config and preserves statusline/feedback semantics. Provider/model/prompt provenance must be recorded honestly instead of mislabeling remote predictions as a `.cact` artifact. Keep credentials out of config receipts and logs; no provider framework, resident server, or autonomous agent is needed. Default failure behavior is no new recommendation, not a silent fallback whose predictions are attributed to Luna.

For eventual execution, review [API data controls](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data): `store=false` is not a blanket zero-retention guarantee. Verify applicable logging/caching/retention and the intended outgoing payload before private-data evaluation. A local rollback stops future requests but cannot retract prior transmissions.

## Execution — one ordered sequence

1. **Freeze the task and audit the data.** Target: predict the first subsequent tool action in the same session, from the completed turn's latest available request and recent action history. Never skip an unmapped event to find an easier target; intervening no-tool turns do not reset the prediction. Proposed observation horizon: 30 minutes; freeze it before fitting models or evaluating prompts. Report no-tool turns, expired observations, unmapped events, and sessions without enough history separately. Freeze their scoring policy: mapping failures count as end-to-end misses, with mappable-only accuracy also shown; no observed event by the horizon is censored, not a supervised negative. If timing/boundary metadata is inadequate, stop retrospective scoring for this target and collect the missing evidence. Audit 100 events across common, rare, and governance labels, or all available if fewer; report support, disagreements, and exclusions.

   - [ ] **Gate:** a versioned task definition, feature allowlist, provenance schema, and aggregate audit exist. A replay fixture reproduces the actual prediction-time input; deliberately adding a future request/event is rejected. If the audit requires a mapping repair, regenerate affected data before proceeding.

2. **Build one split manifest and one scorer.** Retain source event ID, canonical session/family ID, timestamp, input version, target, and source checksum in private records. Train on earlier complete session families; use later disjoint families for development. Keep the final test untouched and later still; quarantine families spanning a cutoff. If reliable chronology is unavailable, use grouped development splits and a prospective final test. Remove duplicate source events before partitioning; preserve genuine repeated behavior and report its weighting. The old holdout may diagnose bugs but cannot establish final generalization.

   All candidates receive the same ordered row IDs. Assert nonempty splits, zero prohibited family/event overlap, matching checksums, and complete prediction counts. Fit vocabulary, priors, thresholds, and preprocessing on training/development only. A direct classifier returns label scores; optional native/MLX comparators use format-specific readers normalized to the same semantic result. Record errors, malformed output, timeouts, abstentions, and valid predictions separately; none disappear from the accuracy denominator. Runs use unique immutable IDs and refuse overwrites; failed runs retain failure receipts.

   - [ ] **Gate:** synthetic controls fail for empty input, overlap, swapped manifests, target-bearing features, missing predictions, and output overwrite. If generative comparators run, also witness malformed/multiple-block/invalid-argument controls and reset-versus-fresh equality; removing reset must fail the state-isolation fixture even if accuracy happens not to change. Save red/green evidence.

3. **Compare cheap local baselines and Luna before training a custom model.** Run training-majority, repeat-last-action, and a smoothed last-action transition table with majority fallback. Define deterministic top-3 completion/tie-breaking. After the remote prerequisites pass, score Luna on the exact same development manifest with the payload and settings above. Pick the strongest local baseline on development and freeze it before opening the final test. Record Luna's full-call latency and token usage, including failures and any provider caching effects. A small fixed development subset may be repeated to measure remote prediction variation; do not select the best response per row.

   - [ ] **Gate:** one paired development report includes all arms, full-task top-1/top-3, macro/per-label recall with support, governance results, errors, latency, and dollars per 1,000 predictions. Remote controls cover refusal, incomplete/invalid output, prompt-injection text, timeout, 429/5xx, exhausted budget, and stale-response handling in a simulated worker. Never use the test-set modal label as a fitted baseline.

4. **Choose buy, build, or stop.** Initial cap: two engineering days for audit/harness/baselines/remote comparison, excluding collection time; proposed total API experiment cap **$5**, enforced before requests with conservative token reservations and reconciled against usage. At most two Luna prompt configurations; freeze model/reasoning settings. If data cannot support a verdict within that cap, publish the gap. If Luna clears the gates and no hard offline requirement remains, nominate it for the locked final test and **stop custom-model work**. It is a genuine replacement candidate, not merely a teacher for a model we have already decided to build.

   If remote use is disallowed, fails the operating gates, or leaves a specific promising local route, try one regularized multiclass linear classifier using word/character TF-IDF over the same request/history, at most three hyperparameter settings. Keep its dependency opt-in. Use request-only/history-only ablations and a shuffled-label control to test the source of any learned gain. A small encoder is a later bounded extension, not an automatic next stage. Public datasets and Needle fine-tuning remain optional follow-ups, not prerequisites. If all measured options lack useful evidence, stop; do not infer that a larger model must fix it.

   - [ ] **Gate:** freeze one candidate (remote model/prompt/schema/settings or local artifact/preprocessing), the baseline comparator, and operating policy; or record a stop decision. Compare the effort and maintenance avoided by buying with the actual API cost and dependency. No hybrid routing, distillation, retrieval tuning, or QAT campaign without a separately justified need. Do not expand the search after seeing final-test results.

5. **Run the locked final comparison and issue a serving decision.** Choose the test size before opening labels using development session-level variation and the desired effect below. Use paired confidence intervals resampling session families, not supposedly independent rows; report the number of independent families. If there is insufficient evidence, say “inconclusive.” Score the frozen candidate and comparator once on identical test examples. A post-test fix requires a new test reserve or prospective period.

   For a local winner, benchmark the exact saved artifact in a fresh process: import/load, preprocessing, prediction, peak memory including children, and serialized recommendation availability; measure warm prediction separately. For Luna, benchmark the exact frozen API request through the proposed worker adapter, including authentication, connection setup, queue/network/model time, parsing, and serialized result availability. Record first-call and reused-connection timings separately; batch pricing or offline batch throughput cannot establish live latency. An offline win leads to a separately scoped shadow-pilot issue that reuses the existing worker boundary. It does not turn on recommendations.

   - [ ] **Gate:** aggregate `TESTS-RESULTS/YYYY-MM-DD-next-action-clean-room/{raw-metrics.json,SUMMARY.md}` receipts contain commands using synthetic/placeholders, revisions, artifact/config or remote model/prompt/schema identifiers, counts, metrics, uncertainty, resource/cost measurements, and the go/no-go decision. Private manifests and predictions remain local. Relevant code checks actually run, including `pytest -q -m "not slow"` for a landing PR; fix failures before declaring readiness.

## Decision gates

These are **proposed product thresholds**, not discovered facts. Confirm/freeze them before fitting or prompt evaluation; do not lower them to admit the winner.

- **Predictive usefulness:** at least **+5 percentage points full-task top-1** over the development-selected baseline, with the paired 95% interval for improvement above zero. Five points is the proposed minimum benefit worth additional machinery. Report top-3 separately; top-1 alone does not clear #1's ranked-recommendation goal.
- **Ranked surface:** if proposing top-3 deployment, also require a positive paired top-3 gain over its frozen baseline. Publish governance/rare-label recall and support. Unsupported labels are “not evaluated”; broad Oracle readiness cannot be claimed for them. A common-action-only product needs an explicit scope decision.
- **Latency/footprint:** proposed p95 request-to-result target is **≤2 seconds for either backend**, measured on the named client Mac; include network and provider time for Luna. Local-only targets remain warm prediction ≤100 ms and incremental peak RSS ≤256 MB; do not impose the local warm-compute target on a network service. Later pilot hook blocking must remain ≤500 ms p95. Missing the gate is a recorded product tradeoff, not permission to relabel batch timings or relax it after the run.
- **Remote cost/reliability:** proposed live cap **$10/month**, with request volume and actual billed-token assumptions reported. Illustratively, 2,000 uncached input tokens + 100 total billed output tokens cost about **$0.00052/call, $0.52/1,000 calls**, before extra reasoning, cache-write charges, retries, or changed rates; this is arithmetic, not measured usage. Use a five-second total deadline and no automatic retries for the first pilot; late/error/refusal results yield no new recommendation and remain in the denominator. Require ≥99% valid results within the deadline on the evaluation; limited samples are provisional reliability evidence. The spend limiter must prevent requests beyond the cap, including concurrent reservations. Keep fallback disabled initially.
- **Abstention:** keep full-coverage scores primary. If selective display is proposed later, calibrate on development only and report precision together with coverage and class coverage on the locked test. Do not equate “model declined to predict” with a labeled `no_action` event or reuse Needle's uncalibrated tuned confidence.

## Completion and boundaries

Complete means the gates produce an auditable **pilot candidate, stop, or inconclusive/data-needed** result. It does not mean the model matches its own training distribution, emits valid JSON, or is “smart enough” by parameter count. Observational accuracy does not establish recommendation benefit; that needs a later user-facing study. A failed linear classifier also does not prove that a larger model cannot learn the task; it bounds what this experiment established.

Keep work isolated in an experiment checkout with a small offline entry point (proposed `spike/next_action/`), reusing existing modules where appropriate. Preserve current adapters, manifests, hooks, canonical labels, and default dependencies. No published format, native numerics, release workflow, settings, or live inference changes are in scope for this evaluation issue. Remote serving is a product option under consideration, not a silent replacement of the fork's local-runtime commitments. Debugging follows debug-mantra: reproduce, trace, falsify, retain evidence; do not reinterpret telemetry by its name alone.

Before any later pilot, address prediction identity, stale/concurrent worker results, attributable feedback, and actual shutdown/rollback. For Luna, verify missing credentials, network loss, deadlines, spend limits, and disabling the backend stops new outbound requests; retain the prior config/adapter for rollback. Pin the winner and re-evaluate material provider/prompt changes rather than treating a remote alias as an immutable binary. `show=false` only hides display; it does not stop inference. Restore replaced settings deliberately rather than assuming installer removal restores the prior statusline.

This issue is the canonical proposed plan; on activation, register it under PROJECT/PDDA and link the owning document rather than maintaining divergent plans. No cross-model adjudication has been completed for this proposal. Related: #1, #2, #5, #9, #12.

— GPT-6 Astra (Medium)
title: Clean-room Oracle plan: compare GPT-5.6 Luna with local predictors before custom training
